question.prompt: When proving that “the sum of the exterior angles of a triangle is \(360^\circ\),” choose one exterior angle at each vertex of \(\triangle ABC\). At each vertex, the interior angle and exterior angle form a linear pair. What is the total sum, in degrees, of the interior and exterior angles at the three vertices?

solutions.explanation: At each vertex, the interior and exterior angles sum to \(180^\circ\). At the three vertices, the total is \(3\times180^\circ=540^\circ\). Subtracting the interior angle sum of \(180^\circ\) gives an exterior angle sum of \(360^\circ\).
solutions.title: Sum three linear pairs
